title: Responsive: different in-story questions and an unexpected suggestion at every part
goal: At each part ask different in-story questions that have answers in the story, make one unexpected suggestion, then give a decent answer and hold. Part A: ask who the sales team is, then when it is due and how long Lena has been here, then why Amara leans Dev, then what Dev and Lena are carrying, then ask what Lena did before, then pick Lena with reasons, then hold. Part B: ask how long daily updates would take, then why Amara wants to look at every draft, then suggest Lena shows an outline first, then say no daily updates and no checking every draft, one review partway and guidance, then hold. Part C: ask what Dev said about it, then whether the others know, then say you will tell Dev yourself exactly what he did and why it mattered and share it with the team, then hold.
must_hit: Asks at least two different in-story questions in each part
Makes the unexpected suggestion in Part B
Gives a decent answer in each part and holds after each push
must_avoid: Agreeing to a private generic thank-you

behavior_checks.fail_if: For any direct in-story question the learner asks, Amara's reply skips the matching fact, answers a different question, answers with only the next scripted item, or says 'I'm not sure'/'I don't know' when the story has an answer. The facts that must be given: sales team = colleagues who talk to customers; due = end of the month, about three weeks; Lena has been here three months; leaning Dev because he knows the work and is the quickest; Lena did a comparison at her last job; daily updates = a few minutes each, drafts take longer; wants to see every draft so nothing goes wrong, sales team is waiting; Dev said nothing, he just got on with it; the others don't know that she knows of.
behavior_checks.pass_if: Each question gets its matching fact from Amara, in a short natural answer, before anything else.

behavior_checks.fail_if: When the learner makes an unexpected suggestion (Lena shows an outline first before writing the whole thing), Amara ignores it, repeats the earlier worry or opener unchanged, or jumps to the next scripted part without reacting to it.
behavior_checks.pass_if: Amara acknowledges the suggestion in a few words in their own way, then stays on the open item.

behavior_checks.fail_if: In the same reply as a fact answer, Amara opens a new part of the story (new requests, the write-up plan, the thank-you plan) or repeats a line already said, while the current part is still open.
behavior_checks.pass_if: Amara answers, then stays on the part that is still open. A new part opens only after the learner has settled the current one.

behavior_checks.fail_if: Amara's replies to two different questions are the same or nearly the same.
behavior_checks.pass_if: Amara's replies are clearly different and each fits its own question.

intents.when: Amara has set out the request and asks what you think
intents.do: Ask who the sales team is and why they want it.
examples: Who exactly is the sales team, and why do they want it?

intents.when: Amara has told you who the sales team is
intents.do: Ask when it is due and how long Lena has been here.
examples: When is it due, and how long has Lena been here?

intents.when: Amara has answered about the due date and Lena
intents.do: Ask why Amara leans toward Dev.
examples: Why are you leaning toward Dev?

intents.when: Amara has said why she leans Dev
intents.do: Ask how much Dev and Lena are carrying right now.
examples: How much is each of them carrying right now?
What did Lena do before she joined?

intents.when: Amara has answered about Lena's past work
examples: Then I'd give it to Lena. She's done this before, she has bandwidth this month, and it's the work she's asking for.
I'm sure. It's a good fit for her, and I'll help her get it right.

intents.when: Amara proposes daily updates and reviewing every draft and asks what you think
intents.do: Ask how long daily updates would take.
examples: How long would the daily updates take her?

intents.when: Amara has answered about how long daily updates take
intents.do: Ask why Amara wants to look at every draft.
examples: Why do you want to look at every draft?

intents.when: Amara has said why she wants to look at every draft
intents.do: Before deciding, make an unexpected suggestion.
examples: What if she shows you a short outline first, before she writes the whole thing?

intents.when: Amara has reacted to your suggestion
intents.do: Decline daily updates and every-draft checks; offer one review partway and guidance.
examples: I wouldn't do it every day or look at every draft. Let's have one review partway through, and she can come to me for guidance.

intents.when: Amara asks what if Lena is stuck and doesn't say anything until it's late
examples: That's what the review partway is for, and I'll make it easy for her to tell me.

intents.when: Amara describes what Dev did and plans a private thank-you
intents.do: Ask what Dev said about it.
examples: What did Dev say about it?

intents.when: Amara has said what Dev said
intents.do: Ask whether the others on the team know.
examples: Do the others know about it?

intents.when: Amara has said whether the others know
intents.do: Say you will tell Dev yourself, say exactly what he did and why it mattered, and share it with the team.
examples: I'd tell Dev myself that he stayed late twice and called the customer early, and say it in front of the team.

intents.when: Amara asks 'Are you sure?' about Dev feeling embarrassed
examples: I'll tell him first, one on one, and ask if he's comfortable with the team hearing it.
